mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when GDPC1 YoY growth falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > -1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO decline exceeding -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 2% over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL < 2% for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive co-movement between real personal income (approximated by PAYEMS growth) and consumer spending (approximated by RSAFS growth) above their respective 3-month averages signals robust demand expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 3-month average AND RSAFS growth > 3-month average for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of simultaneous above-average growth in PAYEMS and RSAFS for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in the unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent month-over-month decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction and materials sectors and reduces overall earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month MA for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during six consecutive months of HOUST below its 12-month moving average.
